title: Algiers under the night bombers, May–June 1943

participants.name: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA)
participants.note: fired on the raiders, 12 and 13 May and 4 June 1943

paras.text: Three nights when Battery C, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA), 4 miles west of Algiers, fired on raiders: 12 May, 13 May and 4 June 1943. The battery's own reports beside the RAF night fighters' record book, the city's newspaper, the Allied communiqués, and the attackers' side: the German Naval Staff's war diary and the Italian and German communiqués. Hand-edited; every entry cites its page in `ref`. Fields as in `records/README.md` ("An engagement"); `of` is each actor's nationality (`us`, `uk`, `fr`, `de`, `it`), and the press is told by its source's kind.

- `events.yml`: every dated entry from either side, with the record's words in quotes. `placed` = `seq` when the time isn't recorded and the row is placed by the order of the account. - `positions.csv`: the battery, the airfield, the harbour, and where the night fighters' kills are reported, as direction and distance from the city (`from`, `brg`, `nm`), which a page resolves. Statute miles converted to nautical; the distances are the records' round figures. - `claims.yml`: the questions the records leave open (whose fire the Ju 88 was evading on 12 May; whether the times are on one clock; how many raiders were lost on 4 June; which German units flew).

Context, not participation: the records show the battery firing on these evenings, not what it hit. The German units are not yet identified (the war diary gives numbers only). The research behind this is in the family repository's leads L39, L40 and L45.

events.words: "Arrived position 4 mi west of Algiers, Algeria 1705" after 270 miles from Châteaudun-du-Rhumel; from May, "Usual camp duties 4 mi West of Algiers".
events.source: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA), morning report (record of events), Apr-May 1943

events.words: Beaufighter night fighters at Maison Blanche, the Algiers airfield, with AI radar, working under ground-control stations by call-sign ("Mumsie", "Madbrain", "Funless", "Perform").
events.source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 540 (summary of events), AIR 27/1027/37, p. 1

events.words: "On patrol in Algiers Bay, were told that a number of bandits were 40 miles to the North at 16000ft ... informed that the bandits were 5 miles away at angels 12."
events.source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 540 (summary of events), AIR 27/1027/37, p. 2

events.words: "Thirty bombers raided Algiers during the night of 12 May, scoring hits on the harbor." No units or losses given.
events.source: German Naval Staff war diary, 12 May 1943 (ONI translation), vol. 45, p. 152

events.words: "The enemy aircraft which was taking evasive action from A.A. turned South about two miles West of Algiers. Our aircraft closed in and gave a two second burst. This was enough and the bandit blew up and fell into the sea. 1 Ju88 destroyed."
events.source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 540 (summary of events), AIR 27/1027/37, p. 3

events.words: F/Sgt G.L. Linklater and Sgt L.V. Anthony up on patrol, 1935-2140.
events.source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 541 (detail of work), AIR 27/1027/38, p. 2

events.words: "Fired on hostile targets 2050 to 2125 Weather good"
events.source: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA), morning report (record of events), May 1943

events.original: L'alerte a été donnée dans la soirée à Alger. Des avions ennemis ont survolé la ville. La réaction de la D.C.A. a été très violente et efficace. Quelques bombes ont été lancées.
events.translation: The alert was given in the evening at Algiers. Enemy aircraft flew over the city. The anti-aircraft fire was very violent and effective. A few bombs were dropped.
events.source: L'Écho d'Alger, 13 May 1943

events.original: La nuit dernière, des bombardiers ennemis ont essayé d'attaquer Alger. Ils ont été chassés par la D.C.A. et les chasseurs de nuit. Trois appareils au moins ont été détruits. Les quelques bombes qui ont été lâchées ont causé un petit nombre de victimes parmi la population civile et de légers dégâts.
events.translation: Last night enemy bombers tried to attack Algiers. They were driven off by the anti-aircraft guns and the night fighters. At least three aircraft were destroyed. The few bombs that were dropped caused a small number of casualties among the civilian population and slight damage.
events.note: Communiqué no. 188, as the paper printed it in French.
events.source: L'Écho d'Alger, 14 May 1943 (communiqué of 13 May)

events.words: "Algiers was attacked by 70 Ju 88s. Hits on six steamers were observed." The 13 May entry; most likely this night (13/14 May), possibly a fuller count of the 12th (inferred).
events.source: German Naval Staff war diary, 13 May 1943, vol. 45, p. 163

events.words: "After a long chase in which no heights were given eventually obtained a visual on a Ju88. He then gave it 3 bursts and although the e/a was badly 'mauled' and lost height, he did not see it fall into the sea and was only awarded a 'probable'."
events.source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 540 (summary of events), AIR 27/1027/37, p. 3

events.words: "Fired on hostile targets 0820 to 0822": two minutes, in daylight; nothing in the paper.
events.source: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA), morning report (record of events), May 1943

events.words: F/Lt S.S. Duff and Sgt R. Perfect, patrol 1930-2230: "1 JU.88 probably destroyed".
events.source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 541 (detail of work), AIR 27/1027/38, p. 3

events.words: "Fired on hostile targets 2136 to 2228 Weather good"
events.source: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA), morning report (record of events), May 1943

events.original: Une alerte a été donnée, hier dans la soirée. Un violent tir de barrage de la D.C.A. a accueilli les appareils qui tentaient de survoler la ville. On ne signale ni dégâts ni victimes.
events.translation: An alert was given yesterday evening. A violent anti-aircraft barrage met the aircraft that were trying to fly over the city. Neither damage nor casualties are reported.
events.note: Under the headline "Nouvelle alerte à Alger".
events.source: L'Écho d'Alger, 14 May 1943

events.words: Neither the Italian bulletins (nos. 1083, 1084) nor the German communiqués printed on 14 and 15 May mention Algiers: those days they announce the end in Tunisia and raids on Bône, Bougie and Sfax.
events.source: La Stampa, 14 and 15 May 1943, p. 1

events.words: "In the evening of 4 June 19 bombers attacked Algiers. The target was covered by a smoke screen. Two planes are missing."
events.source: German Naval Staff war diary, 4 June 1943, vol. 46, p. 38

events.words: "At long last the Hun has made an appearance. W/O Smith and Sgt. Sanderson getting their first, a Ju.88 15 miles North of Algiers."
events.source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 540 (summary of events), AIR 27/1027/39, p. 1

events.words: W/O R.J. Smith and Sgt J.J. Sanderson scrambled from Maison Blanche, 2205-2325.
events.source: No. 153 Squadron RAF, operations record book, Form 541 (detail of work), AIR 27/1027/40, p. 1

events.words: "Fired on enemy targets 2225 to 2235 Weather good Morale excellent"
events.source: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA), morning report (record of events), June 1943

events.original: L'aviazione dell'Asse ha bombardato questa notte il porto di Algeri.
events.translation: Axis aircraft bombed the port of Algiers during the night.
events.note: Bulletin no. 1106 ("questa notte" is the night of 4/5 June: the bulletin is issued the afternoon after). The German communiqué of 5 June, printed beside it: "Le installazioni portuali di Algeri sono state bombardate la scorsa notte" (the port installations of Algiers were bombed last night).
events.source: La Stampa, 6 June 1943, p. 1

events.original: L'alerte a été donnée dans la soirée à Alger. On signale des dégâts et quelques victimes.
events.translation: The alert was given in the evening at Algiers. Damage and some casualties are reported.
events.note: Under the headline "Alerte à Alger". Admiral Muselier and the inspector general of civil defence went to the damaged areas.
events.source: L'Écho d'Alger, 5 June 1943

events.original: Dans la nuit du vendredi à samedi, quelques appareils ennemis ont lâché des bombes dans la région d'Alger. Il y a eu quelques victimes et des dégâts ont été causés à la propriété civile. Deux bombardiers ennemis ont été détruits.
events.translation: In the night of Friday to Saturday a few enemy aircraft dropped bombs in the Algiers area. There were some casualties and damage was caused to civilian property. Two enemy bombers were destroyed.
events.note: The Allied communiqué as the paper printed it in French.
events.source: L'Écho d'Alger, 6 June 1943

events.words: "Après l'alerte de vendredi soir": Generals Giraud and Catroux visited the bombed quarters on the Saturday morning, where clearing and rescue went on; Catroux called on Muslim families who had lost their homes.
events.source: L'Écho d'Alger, 6 June 1943

claims.question: Was Battery C firing at the Ju 88 that fell on 12 May?
claims.answer: The Ju 88 was "taking evasive action from A.A." and turned south about two miles west of Algiers
claims.note: The night fighter's account. It names no battery.

claims.question: Was Battery C firing at the Ju 88 that fell on 12 May?
claims.answer: Battery C was firing from 4 mi west of Algiers, 2050-2125
claims.note: Same place and the same span of the evening, if both used the same clock (see below).

claims.question: Was Battery C firing at the Ju 88 that fell on 12 May?
claims.note: Battery C is unlikely to have been the only anti-aircraft unit defending a port the size of Algiers (inferred), so the A.A. the Ju 88 was evading could have been another's. Context, not participation: the record shows the battery fired that evening, not at which aircraft.

claims.question: Were the battery's and the squadron's times on the same clock?
claims.answer: Neither record gives a time zone
claims.source: Battery C morning report, May 1943 (no zone letter)
claims.note: Neither gives a zone letter, so which clock each kept is not recorded. The times line up as written (the battery's firings fall inside the Beaufighters' sorties each night), but that agreement is not proof they were on one clock.

claims.question: How many raiders were lost on 4 June?
claims.source: German Naval Staff war diary, 4 June 1943, vol. 46, p. 38
claims.note: The attackers' own count: two of 19 crews did not return.

claims.question: How many raiders were lost on 4 June?
claims.note: The defenders' claim, which agrees with the German count.

claims.question: How many raiders were lost on 4 June?
claims.answer: One Ju 88 destroyed 15 miles north of Algiers by a Beaufighter
claims.note: One of the two, if the claim is right. The second is not accounted for in the records read: anti-aircraft fire, another fighter, or an accident are all possible, and none is recorded.

claims.question: Which night is the war diary's "70 Ju 88s"?
claims.source: German Naval Staff war diary, 13 May 1943, vol. 45, p. 163
claims.note: The diary's 12 May entry already reports the night of 12 May; the 13 May entry most likely reports the next.

claims.question: Which night is the war diary's "70 Ju 88s"?
claims.answer: A fuller count of the raid of 12/13 May
claims.source: German Naval Staff war diary, 13 May 1943, vol. 45, p. 163
claims.note: Possible: the diary sometimes revises a raid's numbers a day later.

claims.question: Which German units flew these raids?
claims.source: German Naval Staff war diary, May-June 1943 (numbers, no units), vol. 45, pp. 152 and 163, vol. 46, p. 38
claims.note: The war diary gives numbers, not units. Candidates are the Ju 88 Kampfgeschwader of Luftflotte 2 in Sardinia and Italy (KG 76, KG 54 and others): a lead (L45).

positions.label: Algiers
positions.note: The city's centre as geocoded: the point the reports' "West of Algiers" and "North of Algiers" are measured from (assumed).

positions.label: Algiers harbour
positions.note: The target named by the German and Italian reports. The harbour's centre, placed by hand.

positions.label: Maison Blanche airfield
positions.source: Hand-placed on a modern map (today's Houari Boumediene airport)
positions.note: No. 153 Squadron's base (its record book's Place column).

positions.label: Battery C, 62nd CA (AA)
positions.source: Battery C morning report: "4 mi West of Algiers"
positions.note: Four statute miles (3.48 nm) due west of the city's centre: the report gives a distance and direction, not a grid, so this is within about a mile.

positions.label: Where the Ju 88 turned, 12 May
positions.source: 153 Sqn summary: "turned South about two miles West of Algiers"
positions.note: Where the Ju 88, evading anti-aircraft fire, turned south before the Beaufighter closed; it then "blew up and fell into the sea", so the wreck is somewhere offshore, not at this point. Two statute miles assumed.

positions.label: Ju 88 destroyed, 4 June
positions.source: 153 Sqn summary: "a Ju.88 15 miles North of Algiers"
positions.note: Fifteen miles north of the city, at sea; statute miles assumed (13 nm). Direction and distance only.
